external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders, and which receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: Shoppers have not been given MFA for their accounts.
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker that receives orders from the storefront API, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The password for the database comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_stores.notes: The receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: The shopper signs in to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: The shopper browses the storefront through the storefront API.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: The shopper places orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in orders-db.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.data_description: receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: notification that the order is paid

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The third-party environment controlled by the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because it is described as a storefront API serving browser storefront activity.
assumptions.basis: The source describes shoppers browsing the storefront and placing orders through the storefront API.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface because callers reach it through gRPC, an RPC service contract rather than a web application interface.
assumptions.basis: The source says the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database has confidential data because it contains orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in orders-db.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive has confidential data because it stores receipts associated with completed orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every completed order gets a receipt written to the receipt archive.
